roadmap_payload.problem: A live CDC-managed chat emitted substantive responses for user commands without the required fresh Moscow timestamp, even though the active CDC package already specified exactly one timestamp per user command.
roadmap_payload.fix: Reinforce the existing chat-command-timestamping control with a retained zero-timestamp RED-to-GREEN behavioral scenario and an explicit response-boundary preflight/ledger requirement: before the first substantive CDC-managed response for each user command, acquire a fresh clock observation and require exactly one emitted timestamp; missing or duplicate cardinality must fail closed. Defense-in-depth: Track command_timestamp_accuracy and feedback_loop_closure as dogfood evidence, keep duplicate suppression, and make the missing-zero case part of release regression evidence so prose compliance cannot be mistaken for actual chat-surface compliance.
roadmap_payload.invariant: Every CDC-managed user command emits exactly one fresh [HH:MM DD.MM] timestamp before or with its first substantive response; zero or more than one timestamp for that command is a behavioral regression and creates no authority.
